column2: Which circumstance is specifically listed in the federal dialysis records standard as a basis for releasing confidential information?
column3: Transfer to a receiving dialysis facility
column4: Enrollment with a dialysis ride service
column5: Request from an employer's health office
column6: Meeting with a private benefits counselor
column7: Transfer to a receiving facility is expressly listed. Other requests need another applicable basis for release.

column2: Which safeguard protects confidentiality rather than shielding a patient from observation during an examination?
column3: Discussing results away from listeners
column4: Screening the access examination area
column5: Covering areas outside the exam site
column6: Limiting observers during the exam
column7: Confidentiality concerns disclosure of information. Physical privacy concerns who can see the patient during care.

column2: During handoff, a nurse requests a pressure recheck. The technician repeats the task and timing. What completes the check-back?
column3: Nurse confirms the read-back is accurate
column4: Nurse enters the due time on the worksheet
column5: Technician obtains the repeat pressure
column6: Technician reports the new reading
column7: The sender verifies that the receiver understood the message. Recording the due time, taking the measurement and reporting the result are separate steps in carrying out the plan.

column2: A heavy coat is removed and the scale reading changes. Which entry best describes the verified measurement?
column3: Repeat weight with a note about the coat
column4: First weight with a note about the coat
column5: Mean of the two weights with both times
column6: Repeat weight with calculated jacket weight
column7: Use the observed reading obtained under the corrected condition and explain why it was repeated. An average blends measurements taken under different conditions.

column2: A patient misstates the missed-treatment plan. After explaining it another way, which prompt completes teach-back?
column3: What would you do if tomorrow's ride fell through?
column4: What worries you most about missing a treatment?
column5: What has helped you get a ride in the past?
column6: What would make it easier to contact us?
column7: Teach-back asks the patient to apply the plan in their own words. Questions about concerns, past rides and barriers can guide support but do not check understanding of the updated explanation.

column2: An early ride keeps a patient from completing treatment. What information would best help the team address this barrier?
column3: Ride arrival and scheduled treatment end
column4: Departure time and next appointment
column5: Ride provider and expected trip duration
column6: Clinic arrival and typical setup time
column7: The team needs the specific timing conflict to help with transportation or scheduling. Documenting the trip length alone does not explain when the patient is being asked to leave.

column2: A visitor asks a technician to explain another patient's lab results and says the patient agreed. What should happen?
column3: Refer to staff authorized to verify and discuss
column4: Verify permission, then explain flagged values
column5: Ask the visitor to confirm permission privately
column6: Check the relationship, then give only key values
column7: A reported agreement must be verified through clinic procedures. An authorized clinician handles interpretation even if disclosure is permitted.

column2: When clothing must be moved for access inspection, what does explaining the next step add beyond closing the privacy screen?
column3: It helps the patient take part in care
column4: It limits who can see the care area
column5: It limits who can hear clinical details
column6: It allows release of examination results
column7: An explanation allows the patient to understand and participate. A screen provides a separate safeguard against unwanted viewing.

column2: Who must be present and responsible for nursing care when in-center dialysis patients are receiving treatment?
column3: Registered nurse
column4: Licensed practical nurse
column5: Charge technician
column6: Medical director
column7: Federal dialysis conditions require a registered nurse responsible for nursing care to be present when in-center patients are being treated. A charge technician does not fill that role.

column2: A patient is typically attentive. Which new behavior should the technician specifically report as a change in attention?
column3: Loses track of a simple question midway
column4: Asks for a quieter place to talk
column5: Requests that staff speak more loudly
column6: Asks for the meaning of a medical term
column7: Sudden difficulty following a simple exchange can reflect altered attention. Describe the change promptly to the nurse, who can assess it. Requests for help hearing or understanding language describe different communication needs.

column2: A patient requests help choosing between home and in-center dialysis. Which resource should the technician help them access?
column3: Individual modality education through the team
column4: Home setup training after a modality is chosen
column5: In-center orientation for the usual shift
column6: Group update on clinic infection precautions
column7: The care team provides information about modalities suited to the patient's goals and circumstances. Orientation to one modality assumes a choice has already been made.

column2: A trainee dries freshly sanitized hands with a towel before gloving. What should the preceptor teach?
column3: Rub until the sanitizer dries
column4: Pat fingertips dry before donning gloves
column5: Rinse off the sanitizer before gloving
column6: Blot each palm with a separate towel
column7: Alcohol-based hand sanitizer should cover the hands and be rubbed until dry. A towel is used for drying after soap-and-water washing. Give specific feedback on the observed technique.

column2: A qualified interpreter joins a conversation about dialysis. What should the technician do when asking about symptoms?
column3: Address the patient in short segments
column4: Address the interpreter in short segments
column5: Ask the interpreter to summarize the symptoms
column6: Ask several questions before pausing
column7: Speak to the patient directly and pause so each part can be interpreted. Asking a string of questions or requesting a summary can lose details.

column2: A patient transfers on Tuesday. Wednesday and Thursday are working days. When is the federal deadline for sending requested records?
column3: Wednesday
column4: Thursday
column5: Friday
column6: Following Tuesday
column7: The releasing facility has one working day from the transfer to send the requested record information to the receiving facility. Use the facility's authorized transfer process.

column2: A dialysis patient's blood potassium is rising. Which change in seasoning deserves priority in the dietitian's food history?
column3: Using lite salt instead of table salt
column4: Replacing table salt with coarse sea salt
column5: Replacing garlic salt with garlic powder
column6: Adding chopped herbs instead of salt
column7: Some low-sodium salt substitutes contain potassium chloride. Ask about the product and refer the patient to the renal dietitian for individualized seasoning choices.

column2: An electronic chart preserves a mistaken weight. Which fields should identify the technician's correction?
column3: Correction date and correcting author
column4: Measurement date and correcting author
column5: Correction date and original observer
column6: Measurement date and reviewing nurse
column7: CMS requires the date the correction was made and the person responsible for it to be identifiable. The chart also preserves the original entry.

column2: A patient following a prescribed fluid limit struggles to remember what they drank at work. What support is appropriate?
column3: Use a running drink log for the set limit
column4: Review how the team estimates target weight
column5: Provide common low-sodium meal options
column6: Review scheduled treatment times
column7: A running record of liquids helps the patient follow their existing fluid plan. General nutrition or scheduling information does not solve the tracking problem.

column2: Which starting position follows Project BETA guidance for talking with an agitated patient?
column3: At an angle, two arm lengths away
column4: Face-to-face, two arm lengths away
column5: At an angle, one arm length away
column6: Face-to-face, three arm lengths away
column7: Stand at an angle and allow at least two arm lengths of personal space. A few steps of separation give the patient room to move.

column2: A teaching worksheet uses HIPAA Safe Harbor de-identification. Which remaining detail must staff remove?
column3: Patient initials
column4: Treatment year
column5: Blood group
column6: State of residence
column7: Initials are derived from a name and cannot remain under Safe Harbor. State and year may generally remain, as can a blood group, provided the other requirements are met and staff have no actual knowledge that remaining data identify the person.

column2: Clothing must be moved for an access examination at the chair. What protects the patient from view from the walkway?
column3: Screen between the chair and walkway
column4: Screen behind the chair facing the wall
column5: Gown covering areas outside the access site
column6: Seat facing away from people using the walkway
column7: Place the barrier along the actual line of sight to the exposed area. Positioning or a gown may help but does not necessarily shield the examination site.

column2: Which patient concern is best suited to the dialysis social worker's psychosocial assessment?
column3: Loss of income after reducing work hours
column4: Protein choices that fit the meal plan
column5: Soreness near a new access site
column6: Learning to record liquid intake
column7: Employment and financial concerns belong in the psychosocial assessment. Nutrition and clinical access concerns require the relevant team members.

column2: At break, a requested blood pressure recheck has already been completed. What helps covering staff use that measurement?
column3: Repeat reading and the time obtained
column4: Initial reading and next recheck time
column5: Usual reading and dialysis start time
column6: Prescribed goal and first reading time
column7: Give the result of the requested observation and its timing. A target or prior value does not tell the covering staff what the recheck found.

column2: A patient at target weight plans to skip dialysis. Which risk should the technician reinforce from the care plan?
column3: Rising potassium affecting heart rhythm
column4: Falling phosphorus from lost clearance
column5: Rising bicarbonate from retained acid
column6: Falling urea from a missed session
column7: Weight helps assess fluid balance. Potassium can accumulate between treatments and affect the heart even without weight gain. Tell the nurse about the patient's plan and concern.

column2: A clinic hires an experienced technician from another facility. When is local emergency training required under federal dialysis rules?
column3: As part of initial staff training
column4: At the next annual exercise
column5: At the next biennial staff refresher
column6: After the first emergency activation
column7: New staff receive initial training on facility emergency procedures consistent with their expected roles. Prior experience does not replace training on the new facility's plan.
